blogs.title: When an Informational Right Isn’t Enough—Why AFL Lost Standing
blogs.description:
This post unpacks America First Legal Foundation’s claim that the Office of Special Counsel’s refusal constituted a procedural right violation and yet yielded no Article III standing. By tracing the doctrine from *Lujan* through *Summers*‑v‑Earth Island Institutionals—wherein a mere procedural denial cannot suffice—we explain how AFL’s alleged "informational injuries" failed both causation and redressability tests in full detail.

Readers will see why AFL’s reliance on *Ctr.*‑for‑Law&Educ.
–v–Education Dept.
—and *Fla.*‑Audubon Resc‑v‑Bentsen
‑testisimaset fail when an alleged procedural breach does not give rise to an

concrete,


specific interest.

The post also contextualizes why informational injuries continue facing 
“dead‑end” hurdles.

---
(covers strict Article III standing doctrine)
